label: Real run on this Mac's kind cluster (Kubernetes in Docker, from our own manifests in deploy/kind), with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 4 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged). Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is not right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-b619) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.

fault.name: money-unit
fault.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
fault.cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one
expected_symptoms: the money check fails on payments_match_provider, at the first evaluation after the deploy: for each payment since, the provider charged 100 times our amount ('amount differs')
the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: A payments-api deploy at 22:21:30Z (revision 2) set CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. payments-api stores amounts in cents but now sends them to the provider as if they were dollars, so the provider charges 100x the intended amount. For example, pmt_000237 is for 2067 cents ($20.67), but the provider charged 206700 cents ($2,067.00). The first wrong payment, pmt_000237, completed at 22:21:33Z, 3 seconds after the deploy. All later payments are overcharged the same way, which fails payments_match_provider (51 findings at recheck, up from 48). The ledger still balances and still matches the provider, because it books the provider's webhook amounts. That means the ledger also holds the inflated amounts, while our payment records hold the correct ones. Not checked: I did not look at a trace of the outgoing provider request, and I did not confirm that the payment just before 237 was charged correctly. The money check listing no earlier findings strongly suggests it was.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider failed. From pmt_000237 on, each provider charge is exactly 100x our amount_cents (2067 vs 206700, 1124 vs 112400, and so on), with 51 findings. The other four invariants passed.
payments-api was redeployed at 22:21:30Z as revision 2 with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. No other service changed after the 22:20:09 initial rollout.
pmt_000237 (amount_cents 2067), the first mismatched payment, succeeded at 22:21:33Z, just after the deploy.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its previous revision so CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT is cents again and new charges use the correct amounts. Afterwards, as a separate data repair, refund the 100x overcharge (the difference) for pmt_000237 onward at the provider, and correct the ledger entries that booked the inflated amounts.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The payments-api container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or pause briefly during the restart. The rollback only stops new overcharges. The roughly 51 payments already overcharged stay wrong until they are refunded or repaired. The data is synthetic, so no real customers or money are affected.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback causes problems, redeploy payments-api revision 2's settings. Prefer a corrected configuration over reintroducing CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Then rerun money_check to confirm that new payments match the provider.
